units.anchor: Generative AI may be used with appropriate attribution.
units.fit_note: Permission is conditional on attribution.

units.why: 'We will cover how Generative AI is used within this discipline, including how to navigate its potential uses and abuses'; teaching AI use as a skill (P44).
units.anchor: In class, we will cover how Generative AI is used within this discipline
units.fit_note: Framed as the instructor teaching uses, abuses and attribution in class.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: informs. Coder B: should. 'In class, we will cover how Generative AI is used' is a statement of what the course will do, with no recommendation word, so informs. B's fit_note is kept.

units.why: "Take responsibility for the content" makes the student answerable for what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: Take responsibility for the content
units.resolution_why: Coder A anchored the whole bullet ('What you submit is your responsibility') as one unit with fit_note on inaccuracy; coder B split 'Take responsibility for the content' (P29) from the warning that AI content may be inaccurate, offensive or biased. These are two statements, so they are kept as two units. The unit_stance of the responsibility duty is neutral: it conditions the permission rather than taking its own stance on AI use.

units.why: "AI can produce content that contains inaccurate information, offensive language/images, and biased or unethical representations" warns of flawed output behind the responsibility rule, P31.
units.anchor: AI can produce content that contains inaccurate information, offensive
units.fit_note: Warns that AI output can be inaccurate, offensive and biased but does not tell the student to verify it.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded the warning 'AI can produce content that contains inaccurate information, offensive language/images...' as its own unit (coder A folded it into the responsibility unit). It is a separate statement in the source, kept as P31 informs with a fit_note.

units.why: 'Provide clear attribution of your sources' requires AI use be cited with each submission (P24).
units.anchor: Provide clear attribution of your sources.
units.resolution_why: Coder A gave unit_stance require, B permit. 'Provide clear attribution of your sources' is a condition on permitted use, a disclosure duty with no stance of its own, so neutral.

units.why: Use of AI 'without attribution' 'can be seen as potential academic dishonesty'; nondisclosure is the violation (P28).
units.anchor: Any assignments that utilize Generative AI without attribution
units.fit_note: Anchor is the start of the sentence; the sentence adds that this is treated under the Honor Code.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: informs, neutral. Coder B: must-not, restrict. The sentence says assignments that use AI without attribution 'can be seen as potential academic dishonesty' and be handled under the Honor Code; the wording is hedged and states a consequence, so informs and neutral (as for the other consequence statements). A's fit_note is kept.

units.why: The '[Write-in Option: Faculty can choose to create a separate statement regarding AI use here.]' lets each instructor set their own rule (P04).
units.anchor: Faculty can choose to create a separate statement regarding AI use here.

notes: Consensus of coders A and B (reconciled against the saved source text). Only the three university-layer documents were coded; no Lyle School or computing-unit policy was found and course syllabi were deferred. The CTE page Q&A is mostly advice, so many units are should/informs. Neither coder coded the Q&A items on research-assistance and assessment tools; they are not added here. unit_stance rule used: consequence statements, disclosure duties and verification duties are neutral; table 'acceptable use' examples are permit.
